question.problem: Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{5}?$

current_example.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14151533/assets/e5647c0f19727d1e626e637464cc57444e0bc0f2f8e99a4afd15d3c3631dc3f0.png)

Find an integral expression for the arc length of the polar curve $r=3-\sin(7\theta)$ for $0 \leq \theta \leq \pi,$ shown in blue in the diagram above.
current_example.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta)$ is given by

$$
L =  \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} \sqrt{r^2 +\left(\frac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}\theta}\right)^2 }\,\textrm{d}\theta.
$$

Since $r=3-\sin(7\theta),$ we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}\theta} =-7\cos(7\theta)
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(3-\operatorname{sin}⁡(7\theta ))^{2}+(-7\operatorname{cos}⁡(7\theta ))^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(7\theta )+{sin}^{2}⁡(7\theta )+49{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(7\theta )+{sin}^{2}⁡(7\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta )+48{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{9-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(7\theta )+1+48{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{10-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(7\theta )+48{cos}^{2}⁡(7\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
